I think personal freedom should be defended at all costs and I think the market should be as 'free' as possible without sacrificing regulations that protect consumers and the environment. I think social programs, while requiring taxes, benefit everybody in the end by maintaining a healthy, educated population base that promotes innovation and growth, which ultimately drives the economy. Full socialism would never work, but a hint of it keeps the economy fluid and its people motivated. So capitalism + basic regulatory guidelines for businesses + social programs to make sure everyone has equal footing (education and healthcare being the most important). What is so horrible about that?

I think the social aspect of libertarianism is great, I just can't understand how people think an uncontrolled market will somehow, predictably and reliably, result in a robust economy. The problem is we are all greedy, and money carries an enormous amount of inertia. Time and time again, I have seen that societies, when unchecked, tend towards wealth accumulation to a small group, which gradually drains and impoverishes the populace, leading to a stagnant, struggling society, with a very small number of people leaching from everyone else. Who then, is going to innovate, and create new ideas? Not the ultra wealthy with their yachts. Then the empire crumbles, revolts happen, and we start all over again. I just think we need a basic equal footing (note basic), so that people have the freedom to innovate and create without the massive burdens of life crushing debt, and disease. This, mixed with capitalism, so there is a drive and motivation (ie make money).

The idea that an economy will 'self-regulate' just seems naive to me. For example, say two mega corporations are selling tupperware - one makes their product using environmentally sound methods, and another secretly dumps plastic waste into the ocean. Now when you go to Wal mart, you pick the cheapest one, which is naturally the polluter that cut corners to save money. With how globalized our economy is, and how massive corporations are, you have absolutely no way of knowing which company is 'good' and which is 'bad'. I personally want the assurance without having to constantly worry and do my own investigative journalism to figure out which companies have unethical practices and which don't. Who has the time for that?

Look at East Texas, where regulation has broken down thanks to Rick Perry, and cancer rates are the highest in the country due to the chemical refineries dumping ozone and other crap into the air. "But the people are free to move" or "not buy that company's products" you might say. Hell, I have no earthly idea what products all these chemical refineries pour into and I don't have time to figure it out. And if people just move, well, then who is going to work in the refineries. A simpler solution is to spend a small portion of the massive profits so that your factory actually fits within the environmental guidelines put forth by the government..Then, you're still making money, your workers are healthy, and you can continue business. Another example is the privatization of roads. This has recently happened in my area and I can't say how infuriating it is. In my mind, you pay a simple tax once a year, and you get a convenient, free use of the road - good for all, right?

Anyway, I essentially think there is a constant push and pull - the free market on one hand, and regulatory guidelines on the other. Corporations only care about profit - not your safety or well being. I want to know what I am eating, and that the medicine I take is legit.
Note, I'm not saying the implementation of such ideas is always done well. In fact, it's done pretty poorly most of the time...
